science.title: Structure of NHE6 and its lipid-mediated interactions regulating endosomal pH
science.description: Sodium-proton exchangers (NHEs) are found in all cells to regulate intracellular pH, sodium levels and cell volume. In humans, there are nine different NHE transporters (SLC9A1-9), which vary in tissue distribution, kinetics and regulation. NHE6 localizes to endosomal membranes and mutations in the protein are known to cause the X-linked neurological disorder Christianson syndrome. Despite its importance, the structural basis of NHE6 function and regulation is unclear. Here we report four cryo-electron microscopy structures of rat NHE6 between 2.2 and 3.3 Å resolution, revealing its homodimeric structure, ion binding and remodelling by lipids. We characterize a lipid-binding site between the protomers that accommodates the endosomal-specific phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PI3P) lipid. Using solid-supported membrane (SSM)-based electrophysiology we demonstrate that NHE6 transports both Na+ and K+ ions and that PI3P enhances NHE6 stability and activity. Furthermore, we identify a phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PI(4,5)P2) lipid, which interacts with the C-terminal domain of NHE6 to stabilize an auto-inhibited state. We further demonstrate that NHE6 is non-functional when mislocalized to the plasma membrane where PI(4,5)P2 is primarily located. We propose the lipid-dependent regulation has evolved to shut-down NHE6 activity during recycling of endosomes at the plasma membrane. The sodium-proton exchanger NHE6 localises to endosomal membranes and mutations in the protein are known to cause the X-linked neurological disorder Christianson syndrome. Here the authors report four cryo-EM structures of rat NHE6, revealing its homodimeric structure, ion binding and remodelling by lipids.

science.title: Near telomere to telomere genome assembly of Fujian Longyan Shan-ma duck (Anas platyrhynchos)
science.description: The domestic duck (Anas platyrhynchos) is an economically important poultry species and a valuable model for studying avian domestication and trait diversification. High-quality reference genomes have been generated for meat-type ducks, including Pekin duck. By contrast, genomic resources for laying-type breeds remain limited, constraining comparative analyses across divergent production types. Here, we present a near telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome assembly of the female Fujian Longyan Shan-ma duck (A. platyrhynchos-FJLY), a representative laying-type breed. Using PacBio HiFi (~107×), Oxford Nanopore ultra-long (~35×), and Hi-C (~80×) sequencing, we assembled a 1.28 Gb genome anchored to 41 chromosomes, including 39 autosomes and the Z and W chromosomes, with a scaffold N50 of 79.80 Mb and an anchoring rate of 98.55%. We predicted 18,749 protein-coding genes, of which 99.63% received functional annotations. The assembly showed high completeness, with 99.36% complete BUSCOs using the aves_odb12 dataset, and high base-level accuracy, with QV values greater than 39. Using this reference, we also re-analysed public ovarian RNA-seq data and generated a gene-level read count matrix and a catalogue of differentially expressed genes between high- and low-egg-number duck groups, which are provided as supplementary datasets. This genome assembly and its associated annotation and transcriptomic datasets expand genomic resources for laying-type ducks and provide a foundation for future comparative genomic and trait-related studies.
